We trace this failure to context inertia, where the previous chunk acts as a strong prior that suppresses the new prompt. Furthermore, we find that this inertia persists even when the cache retains only the previous chunk, yet discarding the context breaks visual continuity, which limits approaches that edit the cache. Rather than editing the cache, we propose Residual Guidance (RG), a simple, training-free method that counteracts context inertia with a correction measured outside the cache. Specifically, RG denoises the re-noised previous chunk once under the new prompt without the cache and adds the resulting residual to the early denoising steps of the next chunk, where its content is largely decided and the new prompt is most suppressed. Across settings ranging from a single switch to long multi-switch generation, RG substantially improves prompt switching capability on existing streaming models, including those with dedicated switching mechanisms, while largely retaining visual quality. As it requires no training or per-model tuning and adds only one forward pass per chunk, RG can be easily integrated into existing real-time video generation pipelines.

summary.en: Residual Guidance (RG) is a training-free method that denoises the re-noised previous chunk without cache under the new prompt and adds the residual to early denoising steps of the next chunk, mitigating context inertia and substantially improving prompt switching in streaming video generation.
summary.zh: Residual Guidance (RG) 是一种免训练方法，通过在缓存外对新 prompt 下的上一 chunk 去噪得到残差并注入下一 chunk 的早期去噪步，缓解流式视频生成中的 context inertia，在单次和多次切换设置下显著提升现有模型的 prompt 切换能力并基本保持画质。

papers.title: RoomTokens: Masked Diffusion over Structured Tokens for Indoor Scene Synthesis
papers.abstract: Generating 3D indoor scenes requires a representation that captures object semantics, instance identity, height structure, and orientation while respecting room geometry. Methods that model scenes as sequences of object vectors learn spatial constraints implicitly, leaving collisions and boundary violations to losses or post-processing; semantic-map methods make occupancy explicit, but collapse instance and directional structure. We introduce RoomTokens, a sliced structured-token representation in which each token stores semantic class, instance-color identity, and facing field. This representation allows a scene to be generated as a discrete grid while preserving cues for instance grouping, orientation estimation, and 3D extent prediction. To learn the RoomToken distribution, we propose MDIRT (Masked Diffusion over RoomTokens), a masked discrete diffusion model that denoises semantic/instance-color/facing channels jointly with a shared cross-slice backbone. Architectural tokens are clamped as explicit floor- plan constraints, so the model samples furniture layouts that respect room geometry while retaining instance and object-attribute structure. Experiments on 3D-FRONT show that RoomTokens with MDIRT improve layout fidelity and physical consistency over sequence/vector- and map-based methods, suggesting structured spatial tokens as a practical choice for discrete 3D scene synthesis.

papers.title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generators for robot control by jointly predicting future camera frames and actions, transferring physical priors learned from video into manipulation policies. However, generating future frames before every action makes test-time inference too slow for closed-loop control, while most existing policies remain restricted to short observation histories. Building on Fast-WAM, which showed that video prediction shapes policy representations during training so that future frame synthesis can be skipped at deployment, we present G0.7, a generalist world action model scaled along two axes: extending the context window from a single observation to up to five minutes of history, and scaling pretraining to a large-scale corpus of robot teleoperation and human egocentric (ego) video. Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6x faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging. Project page: https://www.galaxea-ai.com/model-g07.html

summary.en: G0.7 scales Fast-WAM to five-minute context and large robot teleoperation plus human ego video pretraining; Fast mode decodes a 16-step action chunk in 60 ms (7.6x faster than IDM), scoring 70.8 across five simulation suites and 48%/54% zero-shot pick-and-place success.
summary.zh: G0.7 将 Fast-WAM 的上下文窗口从单帧观测扩展到最多五分钟历史，并在大规模机器人遥操作与人类自我中心视频上扩大预训练；Fast 模式每 16 步动作块仅需 60ms（较 IDM 快 7.6 倍），五项仿真基准平均 70.8 分，Galaxea R1 Pro 与 R1 Lite 零样本抓放成功率 48% 与 54%。

papers.title: LeadVLA: Learning Follower-Aware Route Execution for Robot Leading
papers.abstract: Robot leading requires executing a route while continuously adapting to a designated follower. Existing robot-leading systems often mediate follower understanding and physical route execution through explicit states, planners, or modular interfaces; directly learning this coupling through end-to-end trajectory prediction can instead entangle route execution with follower response. We introduce LeadVLA, a structured multimodal policy that preserves the route as an explicit Path reference while learning a Pace for route progress and a Residual for local follower- and scene-conditioned adaptation. To make this problem trainable and measurable, we develop LeadInfra, a configurable Unreal Engine-based closed-loop data-generation infrastructure from which we instantiate an approximately 4M-sample training corpus, and LeadBench, a standardized benchmark with 108 fully held-out closed-loop episodes. LeadVLA achieves the highest task success (39.6%) among evaluated robot policies on LeadBench while maintaining strong route fidelity and follower responsiveness, and transfers to unseen real-world environments without real-world policy fine-tuning. Project Page: https://louiszengCN.github.io/LeadVLA_PAGE/

summary.en: LeadVLA is a structured multimodal policy for robot leading that decouples explicit path reference, pace learning, and residual adaptation, achieving a 39.6% task success rate on LeadBench and zero-shot real-world transfer.
summary.zh: LeadVLA是一种结构化的多模态策略，通过将路线保持为显式路径引用、学习路线进展的速度以及局部适应性，实现了对指定跟随者的自适应机器人引导，在LeadBench上取得了39.6%的最高任务成功率，并能零样本迁移到真实世界。

orgs.name: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Separating Measurement Failures from Defence Failures in Split Language-Model Privacy
papers.abstract: Split-training privacy evaluations fail through distinct mechanisms. Evaluators can overlook an exposed gradient channel, align reconstructions against shifted labels, or deploy uncalibrated probes before testing a candidate defence, while calibrated attacks can also refute real defences. Separating these failure modes alters which claims survive. We conduct a retrospective evidentiary reanalysis across four split-LLM campaigns and two cross-cutting scope checks covering host key custody and variational mutual-information bounds, mapping every recorded claim to one of five admissibility states (breach, non-detection, undetermined coverage, invalid measurement, or out-of-scope inference). Across a 19-configuration exploration, only four of 24 required probes qualified, yet those four calibrated probes still established qualified privacy breaches in 13 configurations, while utility or learning-gain failures eliminated the remaining 6. In a seven-cell defence-redesign pilot, 2 quantised configurations failed utility gates, calibrated next-byte structure probes breached the 0.02 gate on all 7 cells (0.097 to 0.112), and qualified punctuation-property probes reached 0.79 to 0.89, yielding 4 failed and 3 undetermined composite privacy assessments (the latter from marginal null-band excursions on punctuation bindings). Negative evidence against both defence families remains intact. Scope checks further show that shared-key orthogonal wrappers protect passive network captures without hiding activations from a compromised restoring host, and why near-zero variational lower bounds leave worst-case leakage unconstrained. Rerunnable scripts verify 1,522 checks across 122 SHA-256-pinned artifacts while preserving each campaign's native seed intervals and retrospective boundaries.

papers.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) build policies on pretrained video-generation models, on the premise that predicting how a scene evolves helps determine how to act. However, generating future scenes is expensive for real-time control. This motivates efficient proxies for future imagination, but how to train such proxies without sacrificing action-prediction quality remains unclear. An effective proxy need not generate a high-resolution frame; it only needs to provide enough information to distinguish between possible futures. This leads to the design principle behind iWAM: rather than denoising an entire future frame, can we condition the action policy on intermediate features from a single video-model evaluation? We show that the answer is yes. Exploiting the reversible dynamics of flow-matching models, we invert each training future into the corresponding latent noise vector. However, a single velocity evaluation at this latent does not necessarily yield informative features for action prediction. We therefore learn a bidirectional flow map that amortizes future-generation computation, enabling a single model evaluation to provide effective conditioning features. At inference, we sample a latent noise vector from the prior and condition the policy using just one video-backbone forward pass. Across simulated benchmarks and real robots, iWAM recovers the generalization benefits of WAMs while substantially reducing its inference cost.

summary.en: IWAM conditions action policies on features from a single video-backbone forward pass, learning a bidirectional flow map to amortize future generation and substantially reduce inference cost while retaining WAM generalization.
summary.zh: iWAM 不生成完整未来帧，而是将训练未来反演为潜噪声，学习双向流映射摊销生成计算，仅用一次视频骨干前向传播为动作策略提供条件；在仿真与真实机器人上保持 WAM 泛化优势并大幅降低推理成本。

papers.title: Generalized Tensor Parallelism: Powering Trillion-Parameter LLM Training at 10+ EFLOP/s
papers.abstract: Pretraining state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) with up to trillions of parameters is memory- and compute-intensive. Existing parallelization schemes compromise on either per-GPU memory or throughput: data parallelism replicates parameters; tensor parallelism and fully sharded data parallelism (FSDP) add communication of activations and parameters, respectively, to every microbatch; and pipeline parallelism leaves GPUs idle while the pipeline fills and drains. We show that, for linear layers, five commonly used parallelisms (data, tensor, sequence, context parallelism and FSDP) are special cases of one framework, generalized tensor parallelism (GTP), in which each layer's parameters and activations are partitioned and either can be re-materialized with an all-gather before use. In GTP, a parameter all-gather is an optional preprocessing step on one input of a matrix multiplication (GEMM), whereas FSDP implementations typically treat it as a step before an entire Transformer block, which can increase memory footprint and delay GEMMs. The GTP view lets us schedule all-gathers per GEMM rather than per block, issuing each early enough to hide its communication but late enough to limit memory. Our implementation is open source at https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM; with it, an internal 2T-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model reaches \textbf{13.0 model EFLOP/s} (exaFLOP/s) on 12,288 GB300 GPUs with 98\% weak-scaling efficiency, and runs with 1M-token sequences on 512 GPUs. On 256--1,024 GPUs, our implementation achieves \textbf{1.05--1.55$\times$ the throughput of Megatron-FSDP} across three MoE models and \textbf{1.27--1.31$\times$ that of a tuned 3D-parallel recipe with pipeline parallelism} on a DeepSeek-V4-Pro proxy model.

summary.en: Generalized tensor parallelism (GTP) unifies data, tensor, sequence, context parallelism and FSDP, scheduling per-GEMM all-gathers to hide communication and bound memory. It trains a 2T-parameter MoE at 13.0 model EFLOP/s on 12,288 GB300 GPUs with 98% weak-scaling efficiency, and reaches 1.05-1.55x Megatron-FSDP throughput.
summary.zh: GTP 把数据、张量、序列、上下文并行与 FSDP 统一为同一框架，按 GEMM 粒度调度参数 all-gather 以隐藏通信并控制显存；在 12,288 块 GB300 GPU 上训练 2T 参数 MoE 模型达 13.0 model EFLOP/s、98% 弱扩展效率，256–1,024 GPU 上吞吐为 Megatron-FSDP 的 1.05–1.55 倍。

papers.title: Avalon-M1: Reinforcement Learning from Collective Rewards
papers.abstract: We introduce reinforcement learning from collective rewards (RLCR), a recipe for jointly training language models to act as agent organisations under latency constraints. A CEO and up to eight specialists share one policy, co-ordinate through a message board and workspace, and are trained with a common outcome-derived advantage. The deadline makes parallel work valuable when it increases the return earned before the cap. We train Avalon-M1-Mini (120B) across 147 environments. For the trained model, eight-hire organisational execution raises IMO-ProofBench-Advanced scores from 23.8% to 39.0% relative to single-agent execution. Across 12 benchmarks, organisations achieve similar average scores at approximately one-third the derived latency of token-matched single-agent execution and just over half that of eight independent attempts followed by selection. The trained model also outperforms Nemotron 3 Super, post-trained from the same base model, across all evaluations when comparing each model's best tested configuration. On EdgeBench, organisations overtake the single agent after approximately 0.4 derived hours. Over the course of training, organisations develop hierarchies to manage communication costs, invest more in peer review, and alter how work is divided. Safety evaluations find near-universal refusal of harmful actions but sustained declines in external reporting in two of three oversight scenarios. These results establish a shared-advantage baseline for studying organisational learning, performance-latency trade-offs, and collective oversight.

summary.en: RLCR jointly trains a shared-policy CEO and up to eight specialists via a message board and workspaces with a collective outcome advantage; Avalon-M1-Mini (120B) raises IMO-ProofBench-Advanced from 23.8% to 39.0% with eight-hire execution at about one-third the latency.
summary.zh: RLCR 让共享同一策略的 CEO 与最多八名专家通过留言板和共享工作区协作，以共同结果优势联合训练 Avalon-M1-Mini（120B），覆盖 147 个环境；八人组织执行将 IMO-ProofBench-Advanced 从 23.8% 提升至 39.0%，在 12 个基准上以约三分之一延迟达到相近均分。

papers.title: Steerable by Design: Conditional Pretraining for Robust Control of Language Models
papers.abstract: Our goal is to build language models that are steerable by design. Today's language models are pretrained with next-token prediction, which relegates alignment and control to the final 1% of training tokens or inference-time interventions. These models repurpose a single input channel for both instructions and data, leading to common failure modes where the model mistakenly treats data as instructions such as intentional jailbreaks and unintentional in-context alignment drift. To correct this, we propose a pretraining method and architecture that separates the two from the very start, producing Mancelle-3B. An encoder processes high-level semantic features of upcoming text with cross-attention that prevents the token stream from writing back into this control channel. During pretraining, the model learns to rely on these features to predict the next token, turning the channel into an effective handle for steering the model. Mancelle-3B steers more strongly than prompt- and activation-based methods on comparable open models while maintaining fluency, and it withstands adversarial black-box and soft-prompt counter-steering that defeats those baselines. We reproduce this against a more controlled baseline with Mancelle-400M. Our results show that robust control can be built into language models if we do so early and intentionally.

summary.en: Mancelle-3B uses conditional pretraining with a separate control channel to steer LLMs more strongly and robustly than prompt- and activation-based baselines, resisting counter-steering attacks; Mancelle-400M reproduces this.
summary.zh: 通过将控制通道与词流分离的条件预训练架构训练出 Mancelle-3B，使高层语义特征成为可调控制接口；其在同等开源模型上比 prompt 与激活引导方法控制更强且保持流畅，并能抵御击败这些基线的黑盒与 soft-prompt 反引导攻击，Mancelle-400M 上也复现。

papers.title: RoboHarness-RL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for VLM-Based Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Agentic harnesses enable frontier vision-language models (VLMs) to manipulate robots through perception, planning, and control tools, yet achieving comparable performance with compact open-weight VLMs remains challenging. We present RoboHarness-RL, an agentic reinforcement learning framework for improving VLM-based robot manipulation through tool calls. Starting from supervised fine-tuning on successful teacher demonstrations, the VLM further improves through multi-turn reinforcement learning with task-outcome rewards, without relying on vision-language-action models or world action models. To support efficient multi-turn training, we develop LiteHarness, which uses hierarchical memory to keep interaction contexts compact while preserving task performance. With Qwen3.5-9B, RL raises success from 31.2% to 44.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 and from 57.8% to 73.3% on LIBERO-Pro; these gains extend to randomized RoboTwin scenes unseen during training (26.4% to 38.0%). Behavioral analysis further shows that RL reduces repetitive-call rates by up to $4\times$, shortens successful executions, and improves recovery from negative feedback. Project page: https://aim-uofa.github.io/RoboHarness-RL/

summary.en: RoboHarness-RL trains VLM-based robot manipulation via multi-turn RL over tool calls, with LiteHarness compressing context; Qwen3.5-9B rises from 31.2% to 44.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 and 57.8% to 73.3% on LIBERO-Pro.
summary.zh: RoboHarness-RL 通过工具调用对 VLM 机器人操作进行多轮强化学习，配合分层记忆的 LiteHarness 压缩上下文，Qwen3.5-9B 在 RoboTwin 2.0 上成功率从 31.2% 升至 44.0%，在 LIBERO-Pro 上从 57.8% 升至 73.3%。

papers.title: CoRe: Jointly Learning Contextual Representations for Understanding and Generation
papers.abstract: We introduce CoRe, in which understanding and generation jointly shape one contextual representation for images and one for text, trained from scratch. Each representation is read for understanding, conditions the other modality, and is the space in which that modality is generated by a continuous flow from Gaussian noise. With 383M parameters trained on CC12M and no pretrained language model, text encoder, or VAE at inference, CoRe matches a same-data contrastive-only baseline in global understanding and reaches COCO-30K FID 10.10, comparable to much larger generators built on pretrained components. In controlled comparisons at equal data and architecture, CoRe generates better in both directions (text to image and image to text) than a representation shaped by understanding alone and then frozen, and follows prompts better than generating in a space that understanding does not shape. In the other direction, with an attentive segmentation probe, on monocular depth, and when read by a frozen language model, CoRe surpasses the contrastive-only baseline: generation adds information that stronger readouts reach. Because generation runs inside the understanding representation, frozen real-image probes read and steer intermediate states and the model ranks its own samples without extra training. Because both modalities use continuous flows, both also distill to a few steps. Our controls indicate why one representation suffices: understanding organizes the representation semantically, while generation makes it retain more information.

papers.title: SpatialArena: Where Do Geometric Foundation Models Stand?
papers.abstract: 3D perception is shifting from task-specific pipelines to geometric foundation models: monocular depth networks, feed-forward 3D/4D reconstruction models, and vision--language models that predict geometry. However, their progress cannot be measured reliably. Published numbers are not comparable, because every paper samples frames, sets resolutions, and selects test splits differently. They are not robust because the alignment required for every up-to-scale prediction can outweigh the gap between models: fitting depth in the wrong space nearly triples its error, and standard trajectory alignment understates the error of failing methods by up to $2.6\times$. And they rarely cover long recordings, dynamic scenes, or aerial views. We present SpatialArena, an open arena that scores geometric models with the same metrics and rules, with robust and deterministic alignment. SpatialArena spans five tasks, from monocular depth to SLAM. It covers 23 public datasets with 418,929 images across indoor, outdoor, aerial, object-centric, and dynamic scenes, together with Spatial Arena, our own captures with accurate poses and depth. Evaluating 52 models, we find that single-image depth is close to saturation on public benchmarks but not on large, uncontrolled scenes, and that progress now comes from consistency across frames and views, where feed-forward 3D/4D models match or surpass monocular specialists and overtake video depth models. The benchmark, toolbox, and leaderboard will be publicly released.

summary.en: SpatialArena benchmarks 52 geometric foundation models across five tasks and 23 datasets (418,929 images) with unified metrics and robust alignment, showing monocular depth saturates on public benchmarks while cross-frame and cross-view consistency drives progress.
summary.zh: SpatialArena 用统一指标和确定性对齐在 5 项任务、23 个数据集共 418,929 张图像上评测 52 个几何基础模型，发现单目深度在公开基准接近饱和，跨帧跨视角一致性才是新进展来源，前馈 3D/4D 模型已媲美单目专家并超越视频深度模型。

papers.title: A Mesh to Remember: Persistent Appearance for Interactive Video Worlds
papers.abstract: Video world models synthesize photorealistic observations in response to user actions but struggle to remain consistent over long interactions. Coding agents and text-to-3D models instead generate explicit 3D worlds whose geometry and state persist by construction, but whose appearance falls far short of photorealism. Recent methods combine the strengths of both by rendering such worlds into coarse proxies that guide a video model. However, since these proxies only specify where things are, the renderer must invent what they look like as the world is explored, and anything it forgets is reinvented when a surface reappears. Our key insight is that a mesh identifies which surface each pixel shows, across frames and views, even as objects move, allowing it to serve as an address for what the renderer generates. We propose M2R (Mesh to Remember), a few-step causal video renderer that stores its own features on the surfaces they depict, in each object's frame, and retrieves them by rasterizing the mesh whenever those surfaces come back into view. Appearance thus travels with objects wherever they move, persists across revisits, and is shared by every agent that observes it, while memory grows with the surfaces seen instead of the number of frames. Trained only on synthetic data, M2R transfers zero-shot to real indoor scans and to worlds authored by coding agents. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods in consistency across static, dynamic, and multi-agent benchmarks, more than doubling object permanence and nearly doubling cross-agent consistency, while rendering 720p video in real time (40 FPS).

papers.title: DynaMimic: A Physics-Informed World Model for Humanoid Motion Tracking
papers.abstract: Whole-body motion tracking enables humanoid robots to reproduce diverse skills from human demonstrations. Existing model-free reinforcement learning methods either distill motion specialists into a single policy at the cost of performance or train a generalist policy directly using cluster-scale computation. SuperMimic reduces this computational cost through a differentiable world model that implicitly learns the physics shared across motions by predicting the next state from the current state and action. However, this implicit formulation may not fully capture the underlying physical processes. Errors around changes of support can accumulate over imagined rollouts used to train the tracking policy. To address this challenge, we introduce DynaMimic, a differentiable world model that explicitly incorporates shared physics into state prediction. Specifically, its network predicts a contact wrench at each candidate support link and a residual generalized force. DynaMimic then uses these predictions to compute the next state through closed-form Lagrangian forward dynamics. Across 60 full LAFAN1 motions, DynaMimic reduces mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) by 18.6% relative to SuperMimic. For terrain tracking, we give both methods the same local height maps. Relative to terrain-conditioned SuperMimic, DynaMimic reduces MPJPE by 14.9% on A3 Parkour (66.15 to 56.28~mm) and by 10.8% on GRAIL terrain clips (141.88 to 126.57~mm). On a real A3 humanoid, the learned policies can perform diverse skills, such as floor recovery, cartwheel and a box vault.

summary.en: DynaMimic is a differentiable world model that predicts contact wrenches and residual generalized forces, then computes next states via closed-form Lagrangian forward dynamics for humanoid motion tracking; it cuts MPJPE by 18.6% over SuperMimic on 60 LAFAN1 motions and transfers to a real A3.
summary.zh: DynaMimic 是可微世界模型，显式引入共享物理：网络预测每个候选支撑连杆的接触力旋量与残差广义力，再经闭式拉格朗日正动力学算出下一状态，用于人形机器人全身运动跟踪。在 60 个 LAFAN1 动作上较 SuperMimic 降低 MPJPE 18.6%，A3 Parkour 地形误差从 66.15 降至 56.28 mm，真机 A3 完成倒地起身、侧手翻与跳箱。

papers.title: Physicl Scenes: An Artist-created 3D Dataset for Learning Perception and Action
papers.abstract: We present Physicl Scenes, a high-quality artist-created and curated dataset of 6,499 3D scenes spanning household rooms, public interiors, and outdoor spaces. The dataset combines detailed geometry, physically based materials, and carefully composed environments with object- and part-level semantic annotations, providing rich, joint supervision for visual and embodied learning. We demonstrate its value as training data across inverse rendering, 3D reconstruction, scene understanding, and mobile manipulation. Across these tasks, training state-of-the-art methods with our scenes improves performance over alternative synthetic datasets. In addition, we introduce a mobile manipulation benchmark, evaluating vision-language-action models performing physical pick and place in diverse 3D scenes with realistic layouts, and using our part annotations to also score where each object is grasped. Our dataset will be released publicly to facilitate research in visual and embodied AI.

papers.title: Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth
papers.abstract: Looped transformers reuse one block of shared weights along the depth of the network. Recent looped diffusion transformers are trained from scratch, which repeats the full pretraining cost although strong pretrained non-looped diffusion transformers exist. We propose Distill to Loop (Dooop), which distills a pretrained non-looped diffusion transformer into a looped student whose blocks are initialized from the teacher's. We cast distillation as a fixed-point iteration toward the teacher, in which the output after every loop is trained toward the teacher, and each loop is one step of an ordinary differential equation in depth. As a result, one model runs any number of loops at test time without retraining, and the higher-order ODE solvers of diffusion model sampling can be applied along the depth dimension for better results. Meanwhile, because a looped model produces an output after every loop, we also construct loop guidance between the outputs of different loop counts, which improves the generated samples at little extra compute. On SD3-medium, a looped student with about 37% of the teacher's parameters matches the teacher on average over GenEval, ImageReward, PickScore and HPSv2.1 with two to four loops, and with two loops it uses about 58% of the teacher's compute. And on a four-step SD3-medium, loop guidance raises the average of the four metrics from 88.2 to 99.2.

papers.title: Measuring Layer-wise Intrinsic Dimensionality of FFNs in LLMs via PCA
papers.abstract: Modern large language models (LLMs) keep the feed-forward network (FFN) intermediate width identical across every layer, a convention inherited from the original Transformer. Yet mechanistic work suggests layers at different depths do qualitatively different work, raising a natural question: are their capacity demands also non-uniform, and if so, can a fixed parameter budget be allocated more wisely than uniformly? To probe this, we apply principal component analysis (PCA) to the input of each FFN down-projection and measure, for every layer, its intrinsic dimensionality as the smallest number of principal components needed to reconstruct the activation up to a fixed cosine similarity. Scanning 58 open-weight LLMs spanning 14 families and 70M to 72B parameters, we find a recurring middle-heavy profile in which middle layers carry higher intrinsic dimensionality than edge layers; the profile is robust to the calibration corpus, even across English and Chinese, and is largely preserved through post-training fine-tuning. As a direct test that this signal is structurally meaningful, we use it to guide width pruning in a knowledge-distilled student under a matched parameter budget: the PCA-guided allocation outperforms the uniform-width convention by +2.3 points on Qwen3-8B and +2.5 on Qwen2.5-3B, while lower-dispersion teachers show smaller gaps (+0.9 on Gemma-3-4B, +0.5 on LLaMA-3-8B), and a budget-matched inverted control does worst on all four teachers. Across these four teachers, the size of the gap tracks how unevenly the teacher's intrinsic dimensionality is distributed across layers (a single-number summary we call $σ_{99}$), and the advantage persists through downstream supervised fine-tuning. Code is available at https://github.com/naver-ai/lidf.
papers.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. 20 pages, 7 figures, 11 tables

papers.title: To Critic Or Not To Critic
papers.abstract: As large language models tackle longer and more complex tasks, understanding when a critic improves the efficiency of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes increasingly important. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) trains a critic to reduce variance and provide fine-grained credit assignment, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) drops the critic and avoids the bias of bootstrapping from the critic's value estimates. Although recent critic-based methods have reported strong performance relative to GRPO, it remains unclear when each approach is preferable. We argue that there is no universal answer; instead, the choice depends on several interacting factors, including batch size, critic reliance, and task complexity. We study the bias-variance tradeoff in terms of gradient direction, measuring how closely each method's gradient estimates align with the true policy gradient as batch size grows. Under a shared actor objective, we compare GRPO with PPO in control tasks, short-horizon math, and long-horizon terminal agents. Across more than 1,200 training runs, including 96 with LLMs, we find that PPO generally leads at small batch sizes, while GRPO often overtakes heavily bootstrapped PPO and reaches parity with lightly bootstrapped PPO at larger batches. At longer horizons and in more complex domains, GRPO needs larger batches to catch up to PPO's performance. Accounting for training compute, critics pay off at small budgets, but their returns diminish at larger budgets.

summary.en: Comparing PPO with critic and critic-free GRPO under a shared actor objective across control, short-horizon math, and long-horizon agent tasks; over 1,200 runs show PPO leads at small batch sizes while GRPO catches up at larger batches, with critic returns diminishing at larger budgets.
summary.zh: 在共享actor目标下，比较PPO（带critic）与GRPO（不带critic）在控制任务、短程数学和长程终端智能体上的梯度偏差-方差权衡；1200余次训练（含96次LLM）显示小batch时PPO领先，大batch时GRPO常超过重度bootstrapping的PPO并与轻度bootstrapping的PPO持平。

papers.title: SAVERA: Bridging Frozen Vision and Language Models via Sparse Alignment and Visual Evidence Reuse
papers.abstract: Independently pretrained vision and language models may learn shared structures of the same underlying world, providing a foundation for combining them to build multimodal capabilities. However, a key challenge remains in aligning cross-modal feature representations while preserving access to visual information before and after language adaptation. To this end, we propose sparse alignment with visual evidence-guided residual adaptation (SAVERA), a framework that combines frozen vision and language models through bidirectional alignment in a shared sparse space and prompt-guided residual fusion. Specifically, we first present shared-space projection, activation reconstruction and encoding (SPARE), which represents original visual, adapted visual, and textual features through shared soft-gated sparse encoding, with branch-specific reconstruction to preserve their respective information. Second, we devise bridge--text embedding and activation matching (BEAM), a bidirectional cross-modal alignment module that aligns adapted visual and textual features at both the sample and neuron levels, establishing fine-grained cross-modal correspondence. Finally, we introduce prompt-conditioned residual integration of vision and adapted features (PRIVA), a prompt-guided residual fusion module that models vision--language interactions through gating and attention and integrates complementary information from original and adapted representations through residual fusion. Extensive experiments show that SAVERA achieves competitive performance on image captioning and visual question answering while reducing object hallucination.

papers.title: GRAPE-Bench: When Vision Degrades, Does Video Reasoning Hold?
papers.abstract: Despite strong performance on standard benchmarks, video reasoning models remain vulnerable to visual degradation, raising concerns about their reliability in safety-critical scenarios. Existing benchmarks address this concern in part by simulating visual degradation or probing model reasoning with challenging questions, leaving open how well models handle naturally degraded video and whether they can make the simpler judgments that matter for safe driving. To this end, we introduce GRAPE-Bench, which jointly evaluates video reasoning across visual degradation conditions and question difficulty. It combines a synthetic set spanning twelve corruption types across daily-life and driving videos with real-world footage of driving at night or in rain, snow, or fog. Each video is paired with three progressively challenging questions, from fundamental judgments with potential safety implications to demanding reasoning stress tests. Across open-weight and frontier models, we observe ranking reversals between synthetic and real-world conditions and level-specific weaknesses obscured by overall accuracy. Synthetic-data fine-tuning improves Qwen3.5-9B's real-world accuracy from 76.7% to 81.1%, while clean-privileged on-policy distillation reaches 80.4% in a separate reasoning-enabled setting. Through preference steering, we further demonstrate continuous control over a frozen model's trade-off between safety-relevant judgments and challenging reasoning, with little change in overall accuracy. Together, GRAPE-Bench provides a unified testbed for evaluating, improving, and controlling video reasoning under degraded visual conditions.

papers.title: Align the Pair, Not the Sample: Representation Alignment for Faster and Better One-Step Generators
papers.abstract: Representation alignment markedly accelerates diffusion training, but one-step generators raise a question that diffusion does not: \emph{which training path should receive the loss?} A one-step generator sees two kinds of inputs. Corrupted real images come with their clean counterpart, which provides an instance-paired target. Samples generated from pure noise have no corresponding real image, yet this is where the final model operates. We study this question on Priming, which trains one-step generators from scratch by reconstructing corrupted images and then matching feature distributions with optimal transport. Aligning the generative path, the natural choice, collapses recall ($0.45\!\to\!0.15$--$0.25$) in all 17 configurations we test, including five target constructions and loss weights down to $0.05$. Aligning the paired reconstruction path with a frozen DINOv2 encoder instead helps in every setting we test. A short analysis explains this asymmetry: when the target carries no instance information about the input, the optimal aligned feature is constant within each class, so the loss pulls samples toward class prototypes. A control confirms this: aligning the paired path to a random same-class image instead of the input's own image removes most of the gain. Inside the generator, paired-path alignment creates an interface block through which post-training routes noise, and the image semantics carried through it predict sample quality across 16 models. The resulting recipe, \method, accelerates \emph{both} training stages on ImageNet $256\!\times\!256$: it matches the 160-epoch baseline with $2\times$ fewer priming epochs, surpasses its final quality with $4\times$ fewer post-training updates, and lowers FID to 1.30 (B) and 1.155 (L) at the standard budget. A joint single-stage variant trains native one-step generators and reaches FID 1.22 with 115M parameters.

summary.en: Studying which path to align in Priming's one-step generators, aligning the paired reconstruction path with a frozen DINOv2 encoder outperforms aligning the generative path, yielding RePrime with FID 1.30 (B) and 1.155 (L) on ImageNet 256×256.
summary.zh: 在 Priming 框架上研究一步生成器的表示对齐路径选择，发现对齐生成路径会使 recall 从 0.45 降至 0.15–0.25，而对齐配对重建路径配合冻结 DINOv2 编码器在全部设置下均有效，RePrime 在 ImageNet 256×256 上将 FID 降至 1.30（B）与 1.155（L）。

orgs.name: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment
papers.abstract: Model alignment is the primary safety and security mechanism for enforcing refusal of malicious prompts in modern foundation models; yet, existing adversarial evaluations implicitly assume underlying hardware integrity. In this paper, we present FATCAT, the first physical fault-injection attacks capable of eliminating refusal in modern large language and vision-language models. Specifically, we present a non-invasive electromagnetic (EM) fault injection attack targeting GPU-accelerated Systems-on-Chip with physical access, requiring neither software execution privileges nor model-layer access. By leveraging an autonomous Radio Frequency (RF) side-channel trigger to synchronize EM faults to the prompt prefill phase, the attack corrupts safety-critical memory transactions across off-chip LPDDR5 DRAM and on-chip LPDDR physical interfaces without crashing the system while preserving model coherence. Evaluated on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and AGX Thor running Llama 3.2 1B and Gemma 3 1B, localized physical faults reliably force models to fulfill restricted requests, demonstrating that model-level alignment provides no robust security guarantees without hardware-level fault tolerance. Finally, we demonstrate the physical-world consequences of this vulnerability on an active 6-DoF robotic manipulator controlled by a SmolVLA vision-language-action policy. Our attack silently corrupts the model forcing the arm into abrupt, hazardous lunges; in two instances the robotic arm attempted to pinch the paper author -- proving that hardware faults can directly translate into real physical harm.

papers.title: MaskedVGGT: Masked Multi-View Transformers Are Scalable 3D Learners
papers.abstract: Multi-view feed-forward models show strong scalability, but their reliance on costly geometric annotations limits data scaling. Existing 3D self-supervised approaches reduce this reliance through cross-view completion (e.g., CroCo, MuM, Muskie) or novel-view synthesis (e.g., RayZer, E-RayZer), typically learning image representations and cross-view interactions jointly. We argue that learning single image representations from scratch is unnecessary for 3D pretraining methods, as doing so fails to benefit from the continuing advances in 2D foundation models (e.g., DINO, CLIP, frontier VLMs). We introduce MaskedVGGT, which freezes a strong pretrained 2D encoder and pretrains only an added, randomly initialized multi-view transformer, focusing on learning interactions across views. MaskedVGGT pretrains the multi-view transformer through masked self-distillation without annotations: a student predicts targets at masked locations based on complete anchor views and heavily masked remaining views, while an exponential-moving-average teacher provides prediction targets based on unmasked inputs. In experiments across model sizes up to 1B parameters, MaskedVGGT pretraining followed by fine-tuning outperforms single-stage supervised VGGT-$Ω$ training with the same training data, model architecture, and total number of optimization updates. MaskedVGGT also outperforms E-RayZer, CroCo, MuM, and Muskie, providing evidence for the effectiveness of building multi-view pretraining on strong 2D representations. Finally, extending pretraining with additional unlabeled videos further improves generalization, and the learned representations transfer to diverse downstream tasks. These results demonstrate an effective division of learning: reuse strong image representations from 2D pretraining and learn cross-view interactions from unlabeled multi-view data without relying on geometric annotations.

papers.title: Linear Probes Can Guide: Training-Free Control of Representation Generators
papers.abstract: Representation-space generative models, such as Representation Autoencoders (RAEs), leverage pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) primarily to accelerate training and improve sample fidelity. Yet VFMs are more than reconstruction tokenizers, as they feature rich representation spaces that are highly organized and linearly readable. We observe that this removes a key obstacle of post-hoc guidance: by linearity of expectation, a clean probe applied to an ideal denoiser's prediction yields the exact posterior mean of the probe scores at any noise level. This regime, which we call Semantic Mean-Space, turns semantic guidance into a Bayesian linear inverse problem, bypassing the need for training-time conditioning. With this foundation, we propose LiSM, a unified framework for Linear Guidance in Semantic Mean-Space. To validate the framework, we developed and adapted different solvers, and characterized them based on how they estimate probe-space uncertainty and propagate the correction through the representation. In addition, we propose Fit-Path, a solver designed to achieve strong global and local control. Our results in four control setups (class, attributes, foreground, and keypoints) show that LiSM methods, and Fit-Path in particular, provide effective, lightweight control across global and local tasks, outperforming noise-aware and pixel-space guidance.

papers.title: Bathys: Advancing Deep Search Agents
papers.abstract: Deep search is a critical capability for agents tackling complex, open-ended tasks, where solving a problem requires iterative information gathering, query reformulation, and evidence-based verification rather than a single retrieval step. To address these requirements, we present Bathys 9B and 27B deep search agents built around a training framework that spans verifiable question synthesis, post-training, and online reinforcement learning (RL) under context compression. Our high-quality data construction ensures both search depth and reliability: each clue is reformulated as an indirect reference requiring independent retrieval, and retained evidence chains enable verification that the clues jointly determine a unique answer. Curated trajectories underpin a pipeline of supervised fine-tuning (SFT), Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO), and Compaction-Managed Group Sequence Policy Optimization (CM-GSPO): SFT provides a stable foundation for tool use over long horizons and query reformulation; KTO uses binary feedback on trajectories to improve the selection of answers grounded in evidence; CM-GSPO optimizes execution sub-trajectories with length-normalized likelihood ratios on the recorded rollout contexts and reweights sub-trajectory advantages to correct the extra weighting introduced by independently averaging sub-trajectory losses. Bathys 9B and 27B attain 66.51% and 80.49% on BrowseComp, respectively, under an evaluation protocol with trajectory self-verification and conditional retries.

orgs.name: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

summary.en: Bathys 9B and 27B deep search agents train via verifiable question synthesis, SFT, KTO, and CM-GSPO under context compression, reaching 66.51% and 80.49% on BrowseComp with self-verification and conditional retries.
summary.zh: Bathys 9B 与 27B 深度搜索智能体基于可验证问题合成、轨迹构建与上下文压缩下的在线 RL 训练，采用 SFT、KTO 与 CM-GSPO 三阶段流程，在带轨迹自验证和条件重试的评测下于 BrowseComp 分别取得 66.51% 与 80.49%。

papers.title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
papers.abstract: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? We distinguish two components of agentic competence: task competence, the knowledge and reasoning needed to solve a task, and interface competence, the ability to act on that knowledge through a given harness. Across four reasoning and agentic benchmarks, we show that harness-conditioned training yields vastly different outcomes depending on how these interact. Multi-harness distillation aggregates task knowledge from trajectories collected through different harnesses into a shared policy, but this knowledge is realised only when training preserves or improves competence on the inference-time interface. Otherwise, single-harness training can induce interference in interface competence, sometimes catastrophically collapsing performance on a held-out harness despite improvements in underlying task knowledge. To disentangle task and interface supervision, we introduce harness rehearsal: distillation on traces that carry minimal task knowledge while exercising the target interface. Cross-harness task supervision or rehearsal alone yields little gain, but their combination yields gains far larger than either: on BFCL V3 multi-turn with Qwen3-4B, they achieve 8.5% and 32.5% respectively, versus 58.8% together. Finally, on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is more robust than distillation to single-harness training: it does not substantially degrade performance on other harnesses, and interface competence acquired through multi-harness distillation persists through subsequent RL.

summary.en: Decomposes agentic competence into task and interface knowledge, introduces harness rehearsal to train the target interface with minimal task content; combined with cross-harness distillation it hits 58.8% on BFCL V3 multi-turn with Qwen3-4B versus 8.5% and 32.5%.
summary.zh: 将agentic能力拆解为任务能力与界面能力，提出harness rehearsal——用几乎不含任务知识的轨迹专门训练目标harness接口，并与跨harness任务蒸馏结合：在BFCL V3多轮任务上Qwen3-4B分别取得8.5%和32.5%，两者结合达58.8%；on-policy RL对单harness训练更鲁棒。

papers.title: Fractal Neural Synthesis: Constant-Storage Procedural Weight Derivation via Complex Quadratic Boundary Dynamics
papers.abstract: Conventional neural networks store synaptic parameters as explicit tensors whose persistent Flash footprint scales linearly (O(W)) with parameter count, constraining resource-limited edge microcontrollers. We formulate and systematically evaluate Fractal Neural Synthesis (FNS), a procedural weight derivation architecture that replaces hidden-layer matrices with a constant 24-byte coordinate seed Theta = (c_x, c_y, ell) in F_64^3 anchored near the complex quadratic bifurcation boundary dM of f_c(z) = z^2 + c. We introduce a large-bailout (R = 256) smooth escape kernel, four zero-overhead geometric sampling apertures--Cartesian Grid, coprime 3x3 Rule-of-Thirds (Z/9Z), phi-Vogel spiral, and multi-scale Harmonic Tripod--and prove conditional Kolmogorov (K_Kolm <= 192 + c_0 bits) and Shannon entropy bounds. Across magnifications zeta in [10^0, 10^8], C^1 Fourier and lattice-noise bases collapse to post-standardization rank ~2.25 and SHA-256 PRNG exhibits avalanche discontinuity (rho ~ 0.019, 50.6% micro-step retention), whereas dM uniquely sustains both rank (~10.0) and local continuity (rho in [0.81, 0.97], 89.2% retention). Under leak-free 10-fold CV across four zero-scaler-byte non-linear benchmarks, FNS with an INT8 readout surpasses 0-hidden Linear-INT8 by +3.6 to +10.8 pp while delivering 10.7x-129x total Flash reduction (725x-2,773x hidden reduction) relative to converged Float32 MLPs (90.30% Ionosphere in 285 B; 97.22% Optical Digits in 2,598 B; 97.90% PenDigits in 2,598 B; 87.00% Satimage in 1,570 B).
papers.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Reproducible code, seeds, and raw benchmark telemetry archived under Zenodo Concept DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22774934

papers.title: Reproducing the Speech Labels of Qwen3-Omni's Talker: Mimi in bf16, and a Last-Frame Pitfall
papers.abstract: Qwen3-Omni speaks through a Talker predicting 16 codebooks of a 12.5 Hz audio codec, but the encoder that made its training labels was not released, so new voices cannot be trained on matching labels. We identify this encoder from the released model's behavior. White-box regression shows that the codebook embeddings of the Talker, its multi-token predictor and the Code2Wav decoder match the first 16 codebooks of kyutai's Mimi layer by layer. A decoder-based test looks convincing but fails calibration: decoders trained on known labels cannot tell them apart. Teacher-forced Talker likelihoods, calibrated with 13 code language models trained on known labels, do tell implementations apart: the Talker prefers labels from kyutai's moshi package with bf16 weights over every other variant we tried. Loudness normalization and band-limiting of 20% or more of the data are ruled out. Separately, transformers' MimiModel encodes the last frame differently from kyutai's encoder unless the input length is a multiple of 1920 samples. After LoRA fine-tuning on its labels, 44--55% of generated sentences end in a noise burst, and the same frame costs the Mimi-based CSM-1B 119 nats; padding the input removes both. We release the encoding recipe, a label checker and a Talker fine-tuning toolkit.

papers.title: SwiftLoop: Selective Refinement for Adaptive Implicit Reasoning in Looped Transformers
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers advance implicit chain-of-thought reasoning through recurrent latent refinement. However, existing looped reasoners typically employ fixed-depth recurrence, updating all latent positions at every iteration and incurring redundancy when further refinement is unnecessary. We introduce \textsc{SwiftLoop}, an inference-time framework for selective recurrent refinement through position-wise freezing, enabling adaptive computation allocation across both recurrent depth and active width. SwiftLoop learns lightweight freezing policies through hindsight-guided supervision derived from two complementary criteria: K/V reusability at the internal representation level and functional impact at the output level. At inference time, these policies guide adaptive freezing based on observed hidden states. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SwiftLoop achieves favorable accuracy--computation trade-offs over fixed-loop inference and adaptive baselines, with measured inference acceleration. Beyond implicit reasoning, we further demonstrate its applicability to recurrent prompt prefilling in general looped models.

papers.title: Spec$^2$R: Recovering Emergent Properties in Supervised Vision Transformers
papers.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved strong performance across computer vision tasks, but the quality of their learned representations differs drastically depending on the training paradigm. While self-supervised ViTs often demonstrate emergent properties, such as object-aligned patch representations and attention maps, supervised ViTs typically lack these properties, even when trained with strong data augmentations. Understanding the origin of this difference is important for explaining and controlling the object-level structure. To investigate it, we perform a spectral analysis of supervised and self-supervised models, and identify a key distinction: MLP layers in supervised ViTs introduce high-frequency variations into patch representations, disrupting their spatial organization. Motivated by this finding, we propose Spec$^2$R, a lightweight spectral regularization method that fine-tunes the MLP layers of pretrained supervised ViTs. Spec$^2$R recovers object-aligned patch representations and attention maps, while improving adversarial robustness and preserving competitive classification accuracy.

papers.title: Any2Act: Scaling In-Context Robot Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrations
papers.abstract: Robot in-context learning (ICL) enables a policy to perform unseen tasks by following contextual demonstrations, without task-specific fine-tuning. This is increasingly valuable as large language models reasoning at low frequency can specify tasks through demonstrations and delegate high-frequency execution to such a policy. However, methods conditioned on human videos are bounded by scarce human-robot pairs, while those conditioned on robot demonstrations accept only one or two source types at limited scale. We present Any2Act, a foundation model for robot ICL. Our key insight is that a demonstration should be expressed in the camera layout and action space of the robot that performs it (the executor), not of whoever provided it (the demonstrator). This unified embodiment-grounded representation decouples learning to follow from admitting a new source. Any2Act learns to follow once, from robot-to-robot pairs that already take this form in 1.2M real trajectories spanning 10K tasks. Human videos, simulation, UMI, and other robots are then translated into this representation, and source-routed adapters trained on only a few hundred pairs each absorb the residual gap while the pretrained model stays frozen. For long horizons, a training-free tracker feeds only the demonstration window around the executor's progress, bounding the context and rolling back to redo failed steps. From a single demonstration, Any2Act achieves 57.5% success on unseen tasks without fine-tuning, exceeding VLAs fine-tuned on 50 demonstrations per task; other demonstrators retain 74-91% of the success achieved with the executor's own demonstrations.

summary.en: Any2Act scales robot in-context learning from heterogeneous demonstrations using a unified embodiment-grounded representation and source-routed adapters, achieving 57.5% success on unseen tasks from a single demonstration.
summary.zh: Any2Act通过统一的具身扎根表示和源路由适配器，实现了从异构示范中扩展机器人上下文学习，在单次示范下于未见任务上取得了57.5%的成功率，超越了每项任务微调50次示范的VLA。

papers.title: Clinical3D-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Spatial Intelligence of Multimodal LLMs in Hospital Environments
papers.abstract: Spatial reasoning in hospitals requires tracking look-alike equipment, interpreting patient-relative directions, and judging passage widths, yet existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of these abilities. We introduce Clinical3D-Bench, a simulated benchmark with 3,368 questions of eight types on egocentric walkthroughs of 373 hospital-room layouts. Layouts follow hospital design guidelines, answers are computed from the 3D scenes, and paired scene states test whether models change their answers when relevant evidence changes. Videos are photorealistic, and ten physicians screened the layouts. Among 35 multimodal large language models (MLLMs), the best open and proprietary models reach 45.7% and 53.6% macro accuracy, against 40.8% for an answer prior and 79.0% for physicians on a subset, and 27 of 32 open models score below 40% on two-way patient-relative directions. Fine-tuning on Clinical3D-45K, our 44,750-question training set, lifts two MLLMs 16-20 points above the best proprietary model. 3D maps given to the fine-tuned MLLM as input go largely unused: replacing them with another video's, even when they are ground truth, barely changes its accuracy. The proposed GeoJeV instead lets the MLLM compute with 3D: it reconstructs a scene memory from each video, selects 3D operations and their arguments from the MLLM's question state, and adds their evidence to its option scores. It achieves the highest accuracy of all evaluated models, narrowing the gap to physicians.

papers.title: How to build and train your recurrent-depth model: A fixed-point perspective
papers.abstract: Recurrent-depth models are trained with truncated backpropagation, yet it remains unclear why this works. We show that input injection, commonly used in recurrent-depth models, is exactly Halpern iteration, and that a slowly vanishing stepsize provably converges with a backpropagation window polylogarithmic in the depth. The guarantees require a Lipschitz operator, which for SwiGLU leads to a weight constraint in both row and spectral norm, while only a row norm constraint for gates. Based on these constraints, we develop an optimizer tailored to each parameter group, Sparrow, which provides a drop-in replacement of Muon/MuonH with no overhead, that speeds up training even beyond recurrent models.

papers.title: FlashQLA: Efficient Context Parallelism for Gated DeltaNet
papers.abstract: Gated DeltaNet (GDN) achieves linear computational complexity through recurrent state updates, but sequential dependencies between chunks limit parallelism, particularly for long-context workloads with small batch sizes or limited head-level parallelism per GPU. We present FlashQLA, a context-parallel execution framework for GDN that exposes additional sequence-level parallelism while reducing boundary-state preprocessing overhead. FlashQLA reduces boundary-state preprocessing overhead through decay-aware preparation and extends sequence parallelism across GPUs with Dual CP, which shares summary computation across parallelism levels. Workload-adaptive Auto CP and CP-aware kernel co-design further improve execution efficiency. FlashQLA achieves $1.7\times$-$3.1\times$ forward speedup and up to $4.4\times$ backward speedup over Flash Linear Attention (FLA) on a single GPU. On eight GPUs with context lengths up to 1M tokens, Dual CP achieves up to $4.8\times$ forward speedup and $4.4\times$ speedup for combined forward and backward execution over FLA KCP.

papers.title: Factorized Context Attention: From Emulated to Native Grid Probing
papers.abstract: Models read a book, an hour of video, or an image in one forward pass. As the context grows, this pass slows down, loses accuracy, and stops at the context window. Sparse attention is efficient, but keeps the other two limitations. Grid probing, a recent training-free method, recovers the accuracy and extends the reach by asking a frozen model the same question about short local and strided spans of the input, but every question repeats the whole computation, since each span is encoded again. Our insight is that grid probing is emulated attention, an attention pattern reproduced from outside the model through prompts, since each probe only restricts which part of the input the question can see. We introduce Factorized Context Attention (FCA), a training-free block-sparse attention that runs the same pattern natively, as the attention of the model itself. FCA encodes the input once into a KV cache, reads all spans as masked sequences in one batched forward, and uses a stair position schedule to keep every span inside the trained position range. Across long video understanding, long-context text inference and image grounding, FCA matches the accuracy and the reach of grid probing at a fraction of its cost. It gains about 10 points over the single pass on long video and 9 to 14 points on long novels, finds needles in videos of over a thousand frames and in texts four times the length of the window, and answers a later question about the same input in as little as a tenth of the time of grid probing. Native attention thus keeps what emulated attention gains without its cost, all with existing frozen language and vision-language models.

papers.title: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) enables vision-language-action policies to improve through environmental interaction. However, in long-horizon manipulation, sparse success/failure feedback provides little information about where policies encounter bottlenecks. Moreover, repeated full-task rollouts also leave these bottlenecks weakly analyzed and insufficiently practiced. To this end, we introduce ReFocus, a progress-guided multi-round RL framework that alternates between Global and Local RL to identify task-specific bottlenecks and allocate additional practice to them. Specifically, during Global RL, we decompose each task into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of subtasks. Then a DAG-based Progress Reward is leveraged for both policy training and bottleneck diagnosis. Based on the identified bottlenecks, ReFocus selects Adaptive Practice Windows, defining task segments from an entry stage to a target stage. It allocates additional interaction to these segments during Local RL while updating the entire policy. After that, it evaluates the policy to perform the full task for the next round of RL, forming an iteration between Global and Local RL. Experiments on LIBERO-Long and RoboCasa365 show that ReFocus achieves success rates of 97.8% and 51.3%, respectively, compared with 90.6% and 39.3% for the $π_{0.5}$ baseline. Furthermore, we evaluate a real-world adaptation on three long-horizon tasks. On BreadBaker, ReFocus achieves 95% success, compared with 30% for the $π_{0.5}$. Project page: https://refocus-robotics.github.io.

summary.en: ReFocus alternates Global and Local RL: it decomposes tasks into a subtask DAG, uses progress rewards to diagnose bottlenecks, and practices bottleneck windows locally, reaching 97.8% and 51.3% on LIBERO-Long and RoboCasa365.
summary.zh: ReFocus 用进度引导的多轮强化学习框架，在 Global RL 中将任务分解为子任务 DAG 并用进度奖励诊断瓶颈，再在 Local RL 中对瓶颈片段分配额外交互练习，在 LIBERO-Long 和 RoboCasa365 上成功率分别达 97.8% 和 51.3%，超过 π0.5 的 90.6% 和 39.3%。

papers.title: An expert consensus on identification likelihood in NeuroImaging data
papers.abstract: Guidelines on the anonymity of neuroimaging data help manage research data, inform institutional legal and governance frameworks, and support data-sharing workflows. The question of identifiability is particularly salient in human brain imaging because such data are not only potentially personal (i.e., related to an identifiable person) but also sensitive and thus require extra precautionary and protective processes. The identifiability of brain imaging data is also salient for emerging legal and ethical frameworks regarding rights that emphasise the special status of brain data as closely linked to personal identity, mental privacy, and autonomy. Using a combined nominal group technique and Delphi process, we obtained expert consensus ratings of re-identification and singling-out likelihood across 34 neuroimaging data types, spanning multiple imaging modalities and processing levels, from curated research data to maps, matrices, and summary tables. Expert ratings suggest that 38-67% of the assessed neuroimaging data types could be shared with minimal restrictions based on their intrinsic re-identification likelihood, subject to contextual safeguards. The resulting classification enables researchers to engage with relevant legal teams to guide the appropriate and safe release of data, and to determine the appropriate level of protection (licensing, access controls, governance) in line with domestic and international legal requirements, with the ultimate goal of facilitating international data exchange. A website (https://brainimagingprivacy.github.io/) has been created to facilitate the dissemination of these findings and related evidence among relevant parties.

papers.title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles
papers.abstract: The development of biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) with contrastive image-text pretraining has been driven by scaling to increasingly large and diverse image-text datasets. Beyond scaling, further progress can come from learning richer representations from existing data. We hypothesize that the structure of scientific literature itself provides an additional source of supervision: figures, panels, captions, and accompanying article text encode rich relationships across modalities. Yet, treating these as independent image-text pairs overlooks their relationships. To address this limitation, we incorporate these structural relationships into contrastive image-text supervision. We preserve exact image-text matches while introducing weaker positive supervision for related pairs, such as a panel and the caption of a sibling panel. We upweight cross-article negatives of the same content type to encourage finer discrimination. We also enrich panel descriptions using visual content, original figure captions, and mentioning paragraphs. Pairing panels with these descriptions and whole figures with their original captions yields Loom52M, a dataset of 52.4 million image-text pairs spanning scientific charts and biomedical images. Using Loom52M, BioLoom (DFN-2B) achieves 56.82% domain-balanced mean accuracy across 67 zero-shot classification tasks from 43 datasets in 10 domains, compared with 48.77% for MedPMC-CLIP. On BioLoomBench with concise captions and BioMedFlickr, it achieves bidirectional mean Recall@1 of 63.20% and 10.59%, versus 46.37% and 7.55% for the respective strongest evaluated baselines, BiomedCLIP and MedPMC-CLIP. Code, datasets, benchmarks, and models are available at https://bioloom-clip.github.io/.

papers.title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video generation have made automated advertising production increasingly feasible. However, an effective advertisement must faithfully represent the product and communicate its selling points through compelling visual storytelling, which requires more than visual synthesis: it calls for deeper product understanding and strategic decisions about how to present product value. Crucially, product research and creative design are closely intertwined, as the information gathered about a product determines which features can be faithfully demonstrated and how they should be presented. In this paper, we introduce AdProducer, the first end-to-end agentic framework for advertising video creation, transforming concise creative briefs into finished advertisements. Our multimodal agent autonomously researches products through web and image search and translates its findings into selling-point-driven storyboards that guide a frozen video generator. To achieve this, we develop a dedicated data construction pipeline that yields two training datasets, AdProducer-SFT and AdProducer-RL, and train the agent through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with joint optimization of storyboard- and video-level rewards. We further introduce AdCreation-Bench, comprising 305 advertising briefs across eight domains, with two complementary metrics: PG-Score for product correctness and creative execution, and Ad-Score for overall advertising effectiveness assessed by an independent judge. Experiments demonstrate that AdProducer improves the PG-Score of MiniMax H3 from 17.3 to 51.3 and generalizes to Veo 3.1 without additional training, improving its score from 28.0 to 35.9, with consistent gains in Ad-Score, VideoScore2, and human evaluations. Code, models, and data are released.

summary.en: AdProducer is an end-to-end agentic framework that researches products via web and image search, turns selling points into storyboards driving a frozen video generator, and boosts MiniMax H3's PG-Score from 17.3 to 51.3 on AdCreation-Bench.
summary.zh: AdProducer 是端到端智能体广告视频生成框架，多模态智能体通过网页与图像搜索调研产品，将卖点转成故事板驱动冻结视频生成器，经 SFT 与强化学习优化，在自建 AdCreation-Bench 上把 MiniMax H3 的 PG-Score 从 17.3 提升到 51.3。

papers.title: One Phase Is Enough: Sim-to-Real Transfer with Direct Visual Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Sim-to-real reinforcement learning (RL) has enabled impressive robotic behaviors, yet deploying policies directly from vision remains challenging. A common approach first trains a teacher policy with RL using privileged state observations, then distills its behavior into a vision-based student via imitation. However, the resulting student can substantially underperform its teacher. Directly training visual policies with RL offers a promising alternative, but learning task-relevant visual representations from scratch can be sample-inefficient, making one-phase visual RL intractable. We propose DRIFT, a simple recipe for efficient one-phase visual RL using image observations available at test time. Our key insight is to use frozen, pretrained foundation vision encoders, allowing RL to focus on learning control from existing visual representations. Freezing the encoder avoids costly backpropagation through the vision backbone, while its pretrained representations enable real-world transfer from fast, rasterized simulation rendering. Under matched architectures, observations, and compute budgets, DRIFT outperforms two-phase distillation and achieves a 58.8% relative improvement in average real-world success rate across three manipulation tasks. Controlled simulation evaluations demonstrate that DRIFT's relative advantage grows from roughly 9% in-distribution to over 61% under out-of-distribution shifts, suggesting that stronger generalization contributes to superior real-world transfer. Project website: https://jmarangola.github.io/one-phase-visual-rl/

summary.en: DRIFT uses frozen pretrained vision encoders for one-phase visual RL, learning only control; it beats two-phase distillation by 58.8% relative real-world success across three manipulation tasks.
summary.zh: DRIFT 用冻结的预训练视觉编码器做单阶段视觉强化学习，让 RL 只学习控制部分，在三个操作任务上真实世界平均成功率比两阶段蒸馏高 58.8%，分布外场景优势从约 9% 扩大到 61%。

papers.title: EviCraft: Can Minecraft Agents Find What They Cannot See?
papers.abstract: In Minecraft, a common testbed for embodied agents, semantic tools such as mineBlock pick targets from the simulator's loaded world state without a visibility test, so a buried ore the agent has never seen is one call away, and scores cannot show whether the agent searched. We formalize the missing requirement as evidence closure: every decision of an agent system, including those inside its tools, may depend on the world only through facts for which the agent holds evidence. EviCraft is a runtime and benchmark that enforces closure below the agent and makes the admission rule an experimental variable: a perception-grounded regime (G) admits only what is in line of sight or returned by the agent's own actions, and a loaded-state regime (L) reproduces standard tool stacks, with agents, tools, and worlds held fixed. On Survival, the regime effect exceeds the strongest agent's lead: under G, three mid-sized agents reach the diamond in 32%-40% of runs, against 76%-94% under L, and the strongest agent under G scores below each of them under L. In two models, removing only the line-of-sight test closes 93%-96% of the score gap, and loading state only inside tools recovers 70%-98%, so safeguards on observations and queries leave most of the leak open. In open-ended acquisition, the gain from L concentrates in items that depend on buried resources or mobs. Code and benchmark are available at https://github.com/AllenReder/EviCraft

papers.title: Roboclock: A Unified Benchmark for Time-Aware Robotic Intelligence
papers.abstract: Time is a fundamental dimension of robotic intelligence: a robot may fail despite physically correct actions if it acts outside a valid time window, responds too slowly to an event, or fails to meet required throughput. Yet existing robotic benchmarks primarily emphasize spatial correctness and logical task completion, largely overlooking the temporal constraints of real-world applications. We present RoboClock, a unified benchmark for time-aware robotic manipulation featuring 60 tasks across five application domains. Mirroring these failure modes, RoboClock structures tasks around three types of temporal constraints: Temporal Window, Event-Reactive, and Throughput. Furthermore, RoboClock incorporates a Latency-Aligned evaluation protocol that continuously advances environment time during model inference and control-interface delays, paired with time-sensitive metrics. Evaluating over 30 methods, we find that the best-performing approach is the trained VLA, yet it achieves only 8.3% temporal success even on Easy-level tasks, with persistent challenges in generalization and transfer. These findings reveal fundamental limitations in current robotic systems and highlight the need to jointly optimize physical competence, temporal reasoning, and execution latency.

summary.en: RoboClock is a unified benchmark for time-aware robotic manipulation with 60 tasks. Evaluation of over 30 methods shows the best VLA achieves only 8.3% temporal success on easy tasks.
summary.zh: RoboClock是一个统一的时序感知机器人操作基准，包含来自五个应用领域的60个任务，采用三种时序约束和延迟对齐评估协议。对30多种方法的评估显示，表现最好的训练后VLA在简单级别任务上也仅达到8.3%的时序成功率。

papers.title: Rethinking Reasoning Effort Training in Large Language Models: On-Policy Distillation or Reinforcement Learning?
papers.abstract: Large language models have shown strong capabilities on complex tasks, yet how to control their reasoning effort remains a significant challenge for practical deployment. This paper provides a systematic investigation of reasoning-effort training, contrasting reinforcement learning (RL) with on-policy distillation (OPD). We find that compressing reasoning and separating effort tiers are governed by different signals. Length-penalized RL reliably compresses a single policy, reducing thinking on AIME25 by 70\% without accuracy loss, but collapses the tiers when they are trained jointly. Multi-teacher OPD separates them: across 33 benchmarks, low and medium use 58\% and 43\% fewer thinking tokens than high, while high improves on the reference policy by 3.1 points. We trace this difference to the training signal. A sequence-level reward cannot tell tier-specific behavior from shared behavior, whereas OPD supplies a tier-specific target at every visited state, including the decision to stop. Building on this analysis, we show that a single token-level KL anchor on the high tier is sufficient to learn separated tiers within one RL stage, and that natural-language effort instructions make this separation emerge from the start of training, yielding a policy competitive with multi-teacher OPD at matched thinking length. Finally, the separation built by dense targets holds only on the states seen in training: it does not carry over to unseen agentic tasks, where effort acts mainly through the number of interaction turns, whereas the compression induced by sequence-level rewards does.

summary.en: Compares RL and on-policy distillation for reasoning-effort training: length-penalized RL cuts AIME25 thinking by 70% without accuracy loss, while multi-teacher OPD separates effort tiers across 33 benchmarks, with high tier gaining 3.1 points.
summary.zh: 系统对比强化学习与on-policy distillation在推理努力训练上的差异：长度惩罚RL使AIME25思考量减少70%且不掉点，多教师OPD在33个基准上让低/中档分别少用58%和43%思考token，且高档比参考策略高3.1分。

papers.title: Mind the Band: The Hidden Frequency Variable in Geometric RoPE
papers.abstract: Geometric rotary position encodings (RoPE) incorporate 3D camera geometry into multi-view attention by rotating token features according to viewing rays, depths, and reprojected image coordinates. Each coordinate is rotated across a progression of frequencies--its frequency band--yet existing implementations leave this band to inherited defaults, either retaining standard 2D RoPE's top frequency or letting the frequency span grow exponentially with the attention head dimension. We show that this unstandardized setting can reverse benchmark rankings. In novel view synthesis on RealEstate10K, RayRoPE matches the strongest baseline in the 47M model (144-channel heads), yet trails by 1.2 dB in the 25M model (48-channel heads), and exhibits the same reversal when varying head size alone at fixed model width. Populating a 243x range with four frequencies instead of the 3x default at 48 channels recovers 0.9 dB of that gap. Across view synthesis and two-view depth estimation, overly narrow bands consistently blur correspondence, whereas all three projection-based encodings perform reliably when their top frequency lies within 0.3--3 rotations per 8-pixel patch (10--90 rotations across 256x256 RealEstate10K). At the opposite extreme, overly wide bands degrade RayRoPE through a forward-backward asymmetry: averaging rotations over a predicted depth interval damps high frequencies in the forward pass, yet leaves their gradients with respect to predicted depth undamped. Blocking only those high-frequency depth gradients recovers 90--93% of the lost PSNR, showing that forward smoothing does not guarantee backward stability. Guided by this analysis, we distill practical guidelines--setting bands in image coordinates, populating spans in small heads, and avoiding unconditional same-view damping--and advocate reporting and matching frequency bands in future multi-view benchmarks.
papers.comment: 33 pages, 15 figures, 23 tables. Project page: https://bispl-wm.github.io/MindTheBand/

papers.title: Branch and Consolidate: A Unified Recipe for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
